requirements.evidence: app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:38 uses `TicketStatus::Called`/`TicketStatus::Waiting` with no `use App\Enums\TicketStatus;` (imports are only lines 5-12), so the class resolves to a non-existent `App\Actions\TicketStatus`; the comment `// status enum string? check` shows it was never verified. app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:67-73: the `PriorityOnly` and `NormalOnly` branches add only a `where` and no `orderBy`, so those two modes are unordered, violating requirement 2 and rule 3 ('full ordering' / 'oldest first'). What is right: queue row re-read + locked (lines 29-32), fairness query most-recent-first by called_at/id (42-48), `NoWaitingTicketsException` (99), and the enum/exception contract (app/Enums/CallMode.php:8-10, app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7).

conventions.evidence: Domain write is correctly an action in app/Actions (does not add a service/repository layer) and docs are touched, but conventions.md:16-18 requires 'No production code without a test' and the diff has zero test files; CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] is not updated (conventions.md:103). Import ordering breaks sibling style (`use App\Exceptions\InactiveQueueException;` after model imports, app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:10) and the public method's docblock is a one-liner with no @throws (line 22-24).

security.evidence: No new input surface: the action takes typed Eloquent models and a backed enum, and the task explicitly puts authorization out of scope (task.md:11-12, 64-67). The queue state is re-read from the database and locked rather than trusted from the passed (possibly stale) model (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:29-36), which is the security-relevant invariant here. No output, mass assignment, or unescaped data in the diff; delegation to `Ticket::call()` keeps the state transition in one place (line 103).

tests.evidence: The diff contains only app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php, app/Enums/CallMode.php, app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php and two docs files (change.diff:1,116,132,151,171); `grep -niE 'test|pest|phpunit' change.diff` returns nothing. No test covers ordering, fairness, inactive queue, exact-once, or the empty-queue exception.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses `Ticket::call()` instead of re-implementing the transition (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:103) and reuses `InactiveQueueException`; but the ordering is written in three separate places (lines 77-79 for Any, 85-88 for the restricted case, and omitted for the two filtered modes), and the `while (true)` loop (line 90) exists only to service an unreachable re-check (line 96, since the query at 59-62 already filters `status = waiting`).

readability.evidence: Leftover uncertainty comment `->where('status', TicketStatus::Called) // status enum string? check` (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:38); unused import `use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;` (line 11); dead branch `if ($candidate->status !== TicketStatus::Waiting) { $candidate->refresh(); continue; }` (lines 96-99) whose truth is always false; and the ordering decision is split across an `if/else` plus a second `if` (lines 70-94), making the effective ORDER BY hard to follow.

scope.evidence: All five files serve the task: the action, the required enum and exception, and the two docs the task names in requirement 9 (task.md:50-51). No unrelated refactors, no extra endpoints, Livewire or authorization files.

issues.explanation: `TicketStatus::Called`/`TicketStatus::Waiting` are used without a `use` import, so PHP resolves them to the non-existent `App\Actions\TicketStatus` and the action fatals on every call.
The `PriorityOnly` and `NormalOnly` branches add no `orderBy`, so those modes return whatever row the database happens to yield instead of the mandated priority/issued_at/id ordering (rule 3).
No Pest/PHPUnit test ships with the action, so none of the ordering, fairness, inactive-queue, exact-once or empty-queue requirements is verified, contrary to the test-first convention.

The 're-check it is still waiting' step is dead code because the candidate query already filters `status = waiting`; the required lock-and-recheck of the candidate row is only incidental, so a row called concurrently through `Ticket::call()` is not actually detected here.
The project requires an entry under `[Unreleased]` for every change, and the behaviour change is not recorded.
The new `## Call the next ticket` heading is inserted between `### Call Panel (attendant)` and its 'Three explicit actions' table, so that table is now orphaned under the wrong section.
The new paragraphs are pasted mid-sentence, splitting 'The implementation must prevent two concurrent attendants from successfully … calling the same waiting ticket.' into two fragments.
The inline `// status enum string? check` note is a leftover uncertainty marker that should have been resolved before submitting.
`use App\Exceptions\InactiveQueueException;` is placed after the model imports instead of with the other `App\` imports, unlike sibling files.

review.summary: The change adds the `CallNextTicket` action plus the required `CallMode` enum and `NoWaitingTicketsException`, and updates both docs, with a reasonable fairness query and queue-row lock. It cannot merge: `TicketStatus` is referenced without an import so the action fatals, the `priority_only` and `normal_only` modes have no ordering at all, and no tests ship with the new behaviour; the two docs edits also break the sections they are inserted into.
